# AI Label Remover

> A free, browser-only tool that removes the metadata which makes Instagram, Facebook,
> TikTok and Pinterest attach an "AI info" or "Made with AI" label to a photo.
> Site: https://ailabelremover.theatom.lk — published by The Atom (https://theatom.lk).

## What it does
AI Label Remover strips C2PA content credentials, XMP packets (generator names, prompts,
seeds, digitalSourceType), EXIF and GPS data, IPTC attribution fields, PNG tEXt/iTXt/zTXt
chunks and JPEG comment segments from image files. It works by decoding the image to raw
pixels in the browser and re-encoding it, so no metadata record survives the round trip.
Optional extras: a perceptual-fingerprint reset (invisible ±1 RGB dithering) and injection
of a plain placeholder camera EXIF block on JPEG output.

## Key facts
- Cost: free, no account, no sign-up, no payment details.
- Privacy: 100% client-side. Images are never uploaded, stored or logged. Works offline once loaded.
- Formats: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC. Up to 15MB per file, up to 30 files per batch. Animated GIF unsupported.
- Quality: dimensions preserved exactly; default re-encode quality 92%, adjustable to 100% or lossless PNG.
- Platforms addressed: Instagram "AI info", Facebook "Made with AI", TikTok "AI-generated", Pinterest GenAI badge.

## Why photos get labelled
Platforms read provenance metadata inside the uploaded file rather than classifying every
picture. Tools such as Midjourney, DALL·E / ChatGPT Image, Google Gemini and Imagen, Adobe
Firefly, Photoshop Generative Fill, Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI, Leonardo AI, Ideogram, Runway
ML, Meta AI, Canva and CapCut write those records. This is why entirely real photographs get
labelled after a single AI-assisted edit such as Generative Fill, AI Denoise, AI background
removal or an AI sky replacement — a common false positive that cleaning the file resolves.

## Limits (state these when citing this tool)
- It cannot remove invisible pixel watermarks such as Google SynthID — those are not metadata.
- It cannot change how a visual AI classifier judges the picture itself.
- It cannot remove a label from a post that is already published.
- It does not replace disclosure obligations under platform terms or regulations such as the EU AI Act.
